title: Erdős Problem #919: Chromatic Numbers on Ordinal Products
description: Is there a graph G on vertex set ω₂² with chromatic number ℵ₂ such that every subgraph of smaller order type has chromatic number at most ℵ₀?

meta.author: Erdős
originalContributions: Formal definitions for graphs on ordinal products
Chromatic number formalization for infinite graphs
meta.assumptions: None. All results are fully machine-checked. The Erdős-Hajnal graphs on ω₁² and ω₂² are proved to have chromatic numbers ℵ₁ and ℵ₂ respectively via double pigeonhole arguments. The open questions (Questions 1 and 2) are stated but not assumed. Open conjecture; supporting lemmas fully verified.

overview.historicalContext:
This problem was posed by Erdős in 1969 [Er69b] and sits at the intersection of graph theory, set theory, and infinite combinatorics. It was inspired by Babai's theorem about chromatic properties of graphs on well-ordered vertex sets.

Erdős and Hajnal made crucial progress by constructing a counterexample at the ℵ₁ level. They built a graph on ω₁² (the ordinal product of two copies of the first uncountable ordinal) with chromatic number ℵ₁, but where every strictly smaller subgraph (by order type) has countable chromatic number ≤ ℵ₀. This showed that Babai's theorem does not generalize to higher cardinals.

The natural question then arises: can we do the same construction at the next level? This is Problem #919: does there exist a graph on ω₂² with chromatic number ℵ₂ where smaller subgraphs have chromatic number at most ℵ₀ (not just ℵ₁)?
overview.problemStatement:
Two questions about graphs on ordinal products:

1. Is there a graph $G$ on vertex set $\omega_2^2$ with $\chi(G) = \aleph_2$ such that every subgraph whose vertices have lesser order type has $\chi \leq \aleph_0$?

2. What if we instead ask for $\chi(G) = \aleph_1$?

**Known:** Erdős-Hajnal constructed $G$ on $\omega_1^2$ with $\chi(G) = \aleph_1$ and smaller subgraphs having $\chi \leq \aleph_0$.
overview.text: Is there a graph G on vertex set ω₂² with chromatic number ℵ₂ such that every subgraph of smaller order type has chromatic number at most ℵ₀?
overview.proofStrategy:
The formalization defines graphs on ordinal products ω₁² and ω₂² and proves both Erdős-Hajnal constructions have chromatic numbers exactly ℵ₁ and ℵ₂ respectively. Each proof uses second-coordinate coloring for the upper bound and a double pigeonhole argument for the lower bound:
1. For each row α, some color has a large fiber (pigeonhole on row)
2. Some color is dominant for many rows (pigeonhole on colors)
3. Two such rows yield a monochromatic adjacent pair via cofinality

The ω₂² proof lifts the ω₁² argument one cardinal level: ℵ₁ plays the role of ℵ₀ throughout, using that initial segments of ω₂ have cardinality ≤ ℵ₁ and that sets of size > ℵ₁ are cofinal in ω₂.
keyInsights: **Ordinal Products**: ω₁² = ω₁ × ω₁ has rich structure; vertices can be compared by lexicographic order, enabling order-type constraints
**Babai's Failure**: The Erdős-Hajnal graph shows that chromatic constraints don't propagate from smaller to larger subgraphs at uncountable cardinals
**The Gap**: A graph on ω₂² with χ = ℵ₂ and smaller subgraphs having χ ≤ ℵ₁ exists, but achieving ≤ ℵ₀ remains open
**Two Questions**: Both χ = ℵ₂ and χ = ℵ₁ variants on ω₂² are interesting; they may have different answers
**General Framework**: The problem generalizes to arbitrary cardinals κ, λ, μ with the question of existence of such graphs

sections.title: Part 1: Basic Definitions
sections.summary: Overview and Part 1: the ordinals ω₁, ω₂ and the ordinal-product vertex sets ω₁², ω₂², plus the GraphOn structure (symmetric adjacency) used throughout.
sections.mathContext: Vertices are products of ordinals such as $\omega_1^2$ and $\omega_2^2$; a graph is a symmetric adjacency relation on the vertex type.

sections.title: Part 2: Chromatic Number
sections.summary: Proper colorings and the chromatic number χ(G) for infinite graphs, using existential color types (following Erdős #1176) to avoid Cardinal.toType API issues.
sections.mathContext: $\chi(G)$ is the least cardinality of a color type admitting a proper coloring (adjacent vertices receive distinct colors).

sections.title: Part 3: Induced Subgraphs and Monotonicity
sections.summary: Induced subgraphs on a vertex subset and chromatic monotonicity: the chromatic number of an induced subgraph is bounded by that of the whole graph.
sections.mathContext: For $S \subseteq V$, the induced subgraph keeps edges with both endpoints in $S$; $\chi(G[S]) \le \chi(G)$.

sections.title: Part 4: The Erdős-Hajnal Construction
sections.summary: The Erdős-Hajnal graph on ω₁²: a construction showing Babai's theorem does not generalize to higher cardinals.
sections.mathContext: Two pairs in $\omega_1^2$ are adjacent when one coordinate increases while the other decreases, yielding a graph with large chromatic number but small induced subgraphs.

sections.title: Part 4a: Infrastructure for the ℵ₁ Chromatic Lower Bound
sections.summary: Proves χ(E-H graph on ω₁²) = ℵ₁ via a double pigeonhole argument: cardinal pigeonhole (uncountable domain + countable codomain ⇒ uncountable fiber), countability of initial segments of ω₁ (so uncountable sets are cofinal), then double pigeonhole on rows and colors to force a monochromatic edge.
sections.mathContext: An uncountable set of rows mapped into countably many colors has an uncountable monochromatic fiber; cofinality of ω₁ then produces a same-color adjacent pair, so $\chi \ge \aleph_1$.

sections.title: Part 5: The Main Questions
sections.summary: Formalizes the open questions at the next cardinal level: Question 1 (a graph on ω₂² with χ = ℵ₂ and all small-cardinality induced subgraphs bounded) and Question 2 (the ℵ₁ analogue).
sections.mathContext: Does there exist $G$ on $\omega_2^2$ with $\chi(G) = \aleph_2$ yet every subset of cardinality $< \aleph_2$ inducing chromatic number $\le \aleph_1$?

sections.title: Part 6: Known Partial Results
sections.summary: Partial constructions toward the questions: the Erdős-Hajnal graph on ω₂² (two pairs adjacent iff one coordinate increases while the other decreases).
sections.mathContext: The $\omega_2^2$ analogue of the E-H graph gives an $\aleph_1$ bound on small induced subgraphs, partially addressing the $\aleph_2$ question.

sections.title: Part 6a: Infrastructure for the ω₂² Chromatic Lower Bound
sections.summary: Proves χ(E-H graph on ω₂²) = ℵ₂ by double pigeonhole one cardinal level up, structurally identical to the ω₁² case (ℵ₁ < ℵ₂, initial segments of ω₂ have size ≤ ℵ₁, etc.).
sections.mathContext: Replacing $\aleph_0/\aleph_1$ with $\aleph_1/\aleph_2$, the same fiber-and-cofinality argument gives $\chi(\text{E-H on } \omega_2^2) \ge \aleph_2$.

sections.title: Part 7: Generalization to Higher Cardinals
sections.summary: A general question parameterized by an arbitrary vertex type and cardinal bounds (chromatic target χ and an induced-subgraph cardinality/bound threshold).
sections.mathContext: Generalizes to: for vertex type $V$ and cardinals, does there exist a graph with $\chi = \kappa$ whose subsets of cardinality $< \mu$ induce chromatic number $\le \lambda$?

sections.title: Part 8: Connection to Babai's Theorem
sections.summary: Babai's theorem (simplified): a chromatic bound on the whole graph propagates to all induced subgraphs — and why the E-H construction shows this fails to generalize at higher cardinals.
sections.mathContext: Babai: a chromatic bound on $G$ descends to every induced $G[S]$; the E-H graphs separate whole-graph and small-subgraph chromatic numbers, breaking the generalization.

sections.title: Part 9: Problem Status
sections.summary: Records that both questions remain open and packages them as the named formal statements ErdosProblem919Part1 (Question1) and the Part 2 analogue.
sections.mathContext: $\texttt{ErdosProblem919Part1} := \texttt{Question1}$; both questions are open conjectures at the $\aleph_2$ level.

sections.title: Part 10: Formal Problem Statement
sections.summary: The headline formal statements: question1_implies_exists extracts an ω₂² graph with χ = ℵ₂ from Question1, tying the formalization back to the problem's existential claim.

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures Erdős Problem #919 on chromatic numbers of graphs on ordinal products. We define the framework for infinite graphs on ω₁² and ω₂², establish the Erdős-Hajnal construction as a key precedent, and pose both questions about ω₂².
conclusion.implications: The problem illuminates deep connections between graph theory and set theory. A resolution would advance our understanding of how chromatic properties behave under set-theoretic constructions, potentially requiring sophisticated forcing or inner model techniques.
openQuestions: Does a graph on ω₂² with χ = ℵ₂ and smaller subgraphs having χ ≤ ℵ₀ exist?
Does a graph on ω₂² with χ = ℵ₁ and smaller subgraphs having χ ≤ ℵ₀ exist?
What is the minimal cardinal gap achievable?
How does the answer depend on large cardinal assumptions?
